about.title: Perris Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely announces itself. One moment you are stepping out of a Perris Boulevard grocery store, and the next you are on the pavement with a wrist that will not bend right. Property owners in Perris and across Riverside County have a duty to keep walkways, stairwells, and parking areas reasonably safe, and to warn visitors about hazards they knew about or should have discovered. California law calls that "notice," and proving it is usually the heart of a premises case. That is where LawProactive comes in. We are a free connection service, not a law firm. Tell us what happened and we match you with an independent attorney who handles slip and fall claims in this area and works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Whether your fall happened at an apartment complex off 4th Street, a restaurant lot near the Ramona Expressway, or a neighbor's home, the same steps matter: photograph the hazard, get treated, and act before California's two-year deadline passes.

whyChoose.title: Why Perris Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Attorneys who understand the notice requirement
items.desc: In California, you generally have to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and did nothing. The attorneys in our network know how to build that proof through inspection logs, prior complaints, and witness accounts.

items.title: Help preserving video before it disappears
items.desc: Many Perris businesses record their aisles and parking lots, but footage is often overwritten within days. A quick connection means a preservation letter can go out early, before key evidence is lost.

items.title: Clear guidance on deadlines and shared fault
items.desc: Most premises claims carry a two-year limit, but claims against a city or county are far shorter. California also uses pure comparative fault, so a claim can still proceed even if you were partly responsible.

items.question: I fell at a Perris city park or a Riverside County building. Is the deadline different?
items.answer: Yes, and it is much shorter. When the property is owned or maintained by a public entity, California generally requires a formal government claim to be filed first, often within six months of the injury, before any lawsuit can be brought. Missing that window can end the claim entirely, so it is worth speaking with an attorney right away rather than waiting to see how your injuries heal.

items.question: The store says I wasn't paying attention. Does that mean I have no case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California follows pure comparative fault, which means your recovery can be reduced by your share of responsibility but is not automatically eliminated. If a spill sat on the floor for an hour with no cone or sign, the owner's failure to warn still matters, even if you were looking at your phone. An attorney can weigh how those facts fit together in your situation.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in Perris?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems manageable, because fall injuries often worsen over the following days. Photograph the exact spot, the lighting, and anything that caused the fall, and write down names of anyone who saw it. Ask the property to keep any surveillance footage, and hold onto the shoes you were wearing. Then reach out to us so an attorney can send a formal preservation request while the evidence still exists.
